claims.text: Atomic short-range order governs or mediates the magnetostructural transition in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
The density of nanoscale twin boundaries governs or mediates the magnetostructural transition in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
A mild post-deposition thermal treatment can promote a three-dimensional hierarchical twin network.
A mild post-deposition thermal treatment can induce targeted atomic short-range order.
The proposed annealing treatment can modify twin density and short-range order without changing the overall phase.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is a single-phase ordered hexagonal material.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
The as-deposited material has a low surface-to-volume ratio comparable to arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons.
An engineered hierarchical twin network reversibly accommodates magnetostructural transformation strain.
Reversible strain accommodation by the twin network lowers the energy barriers of the magnetostructural transition.
The annealed samples will have a broader magnetocaloric peak or transition-temperature range than the as-deposited samples.
The annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis width than the as-deposited samples during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The annealed samples will retain a magnetocaloric entropy change similar to that of the as-deposited samples.
The annealing-induced internal microstructure will enhance the material's surface-to-volume characteristics.
The claimed increase in surface-to-volume characteristics will produce faster heat exchange during cooling cycles.
The predicted benefit is confined to low applied fields, temperatures near the transition, and sufficiently mild treatments.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration can eliminate the desired twin or short-range-order state or cause loss of the ordered phase.

contradictions.description: The intervention attributes targeted short-range order to thermal annealing, whereas the structural mediator calls it mechanically induced short-range order; no mechanical treatment is included.
The intervention is an internal annealing treatment that is not specified to change sample geometry or porosity, yet the predicted outcome asserts enhanced surface-to-volume characteristics.
